name: Ride-On Floor Sweeper
definition: A commercial sweeper with an integrated seated operator position used during normal sweeping, with model-specific brush, hopper, dumping, dust-control, traction and power systems.
includedScope: Battery and engine ride-on floor sweepers
Low-dump and high-dump commercial vacuum sweepers
headline: Ride-on floor sweeper types, hopper dumping, route geometry and buyer checks
description: This profile explains seated ride-on sweepers, brush and filtration systems, low- and high-dump hoppers, turning and overhead constraints, representative models and procurement verification.
metaDescription: Ride-on floor sweeper technical guide covering low- and high-dump types, dust control, specifications, models, route fit and buyer checks.
disclaimer: This independent category reference is not model-specific purchasing, safety, hazardous-material, textile-care or repair advice. Confirm the current manual, exact configuration, serial range, local compliance and service terms before procurement or use.

keyFacts.label: Category boundary
keyFacts.evidence: Reviewed official sources classify the named machines as ride-on sweepers.
keyFacts.scope: Named commercial models; stand-on machines are excluded.

keyFacts.label: Dumping formats
keyFacts.value: Manual low dump or powered high dump
keyFacts.evidence: Official specifications distinguish low- and high-dump configurations.

keyFacts.label: Route constraints
keyFacts.value: Turning, slope, overhead and operating mass are configuration-specific
keyFacts.evidence: Manufacturer sources publish dimensions, turning and selected operating limits.

keyFacts.label: Buyer verification
keyFacts.value: Witness turning, braking, slopes, dumping, filter service and a full representative route
keyFacts.evidence: Official specifications use model- and configuration-specific reporting boundaries.
keyFacts.scope: Quoted regional configuration and actual buyer site.

systemFlow.name: Edge gathering
systemFlow.role: Extends the sweeping path and gathers edge debris.
systemFlow.evidence: Official sources publish single- and dual-side-brush paths.

systemFlow.name: Main sweeping
systemFlow.role: Transfers debris into the hopper path.
systemFlow.evidence: Manufacturer sources identify main brush systems.

systemFlow.name: Collection and dump
systemFlow.evidence: Official pages describe low- or high-dump arrangements.

systemFlow.name: Dust and propulsion
systemFlow.role: Controls dust and moves the seated machine.
systemFlow.evidence: Official sources publish filtration and power-system details.

variants.name: Compact low dump
variants.operatorRelationship: Seated driving with manual hopper removal
variants.spaceConstraints: Compact turning and storage still required
variants.limitations: Manual dumping can add labor and exposure.
variants.evidence: TASKI and Tennant publish compact ride-on configurations.

variants.name: High dump
variants.operatorRelationship: Seated operation with powered hopper lift
variants.spaceConstraints: Dump height and overhead envelope increase
variants.limitations: Raised-hopper stability and clearance require exact manual limits.
variants.evidence: Tennant and Kärcher describe high-dump systems.

variants.name: Battery or engine power
variants.taskScale: Duty cycle and environment determine power choice
variants.spaceConstraints: Charging, fuel, ventilation and emissions differ
variants.limitations: Indoor suitability cannot be inferred from size.
variants.evidence: Official ranges disclose configuration-specific power systems.
